newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler buys heavy truck business from Ford.
newsitem.headline: Daimler buys heavy truck business from Ford.

text.p: German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday its U.S. truck unit Freightliner has bought the heavy truck business of Ford Motor Co in a bid to increase its North American market share.
Daimler said both companies signed a letter of intent for the deal on Wednesday but terms were not disclosed.
The deal calls for Freightliner to buy Ford's heavy truck business, including Ford's "HN80" truck project that was launched in 1996, Daimler said in a statement.
But Ford will remain in the light and mid-sized markets while Freightliner gains more market share in the 8 to 15 tonne vehicle market for construction and distribution trucks.
Freightliner, acquired by Daimler in 1981, said it will operate separate sales divisions with separate dealers for Freightliner and the products acquired from Ford.
Daimler noted that the deal will add more than $1 billion to its 1996 revenues of about $4.8 billion. The Portland, Oregon-based group sold 77,148 vehicles last year.
Ford's technology, tooling and assembly equipment for the sector will be acquired by Freightliner and production of the "HN80" truck will continue at Freightliner facilities.

Ford's heavy-truck parts business and the product rights in the predecessor "L-Series" truck series and the Ford cargo trucks will also pass from Ford to Freightliner. Ford heavy trucks are sold in the United States, Canada and Australia.
Daimler-Benz said the deal will allow Daimler to broaden its top position in the North American truck market, a segment he said was profitable for the Stuttgart-based group.
"We see significant strategic values in a second heavy-truck line that complements Freightliner's existing business," said Kurt Lauk, the director of Daimler's commercial vehicle division.
